“Listen here, Bond, your next mission is to travel to Brussels and help the European Commission learn how to detect deepfakes.”
“Sounds dangerous, M. Anything I need to get from Q before I go? A pen that fires poison darts? A car that can fly?”
“You need to sign up to the Transparency Register, and allow extra time to get through security at the Eurostar terminal. That blasted EU entry/exit system is a nightmare.”
We now know that Robert Pattinson will be the next James Bond but can being the world’s most famous spy top the time he was heavily featured in a webinar organized by the European Commission entitled “Forensic AI in E-evidence”?
The session, held in April 2022, looked at how to fight deepfakes using technology and was given by Siwei Lyu, a professor in the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at the University at Buffalo in the U.S.
The presentation, the slides of which were seen by POLITICO, repeatedly asked the question “Is this Robert Pattinson?” alongside images of the actor and information on how to spot deepfakes — images, video and audio that are digitally generated or modified to make a person say or do things that they have not done.
In addition, two films starring Pattinson — 2012’s “Bel Ami” and 2018’s “High Life” — received support from Creative Europe MEDIA, the EU’s funding program for supporting the film and TV industries.
